title.narrative: Fourth Phase of the Central Asia Regional Links Program

description.narrative: The Fourth Phase of the Central Asia Regional Links (CARs) program, a series of projects (SOP) in multiple countries (borrowers), has the following components.Component 1: Improve regional connections in Sughd and GBAO regions (US$89 million equivalent from IDA; US$1 million from PACT Trust Fund). Activities to be financed under this component include: (i) rehabilitation of a 50.5 km long, Category I and III roads in Sughd in four sections (estimated at US$37.0 million); (ii) construction of Khorog bridge and tunnels/galleries and bridges around Barsem Village in GBAO to enhance the resilience of the road connectivity from climate hazards such as mudslides and avalanches (estimated US$46.7 million); (iii) provision of construction supervision services for road construction and rehabilitation works (estimated US$4.3 million); and (iv) preparation of feasibility studies for improvement of regional road connectivity for Sughd, Khatlon and GBAO regions as basis for potential lending operation (CARs-5), to be partially financed by PACT Trust Fund (estimated US$2.0 million).Component 2: Improve road asset preservation and road safety (US$20 million equivalent) comprises two sub-components.Sub-Component 2a Improve road asset preservation (US$8 million equivalent) will finance (i) supply and installation of weigh-in-motion (WIM) systems to preserve road assets, (ii) installation and commission of software packages for recording, storage and analysis of road network condition data, development of prioritized maintenance planning, optimized to allow for budget constraints, and annual maintenance plans, and (iii) training on the installed systems. Activities under this component have been carefully coordinated with other development partners.Sub-Component 2b Improve Road Safety (US$12.0 million equivalent) will finance three activities. (i) Support the Department of State Automobile Inspection to enforce use of 4-wheel vehicle safety belts, through a legal review and regulatory reforms, publicity campaign to warn of start of enforcement, and design of, and implement support for, an enforcement campaign. (ii) Retrofit or construct safety barriers along selected road sections in severe mountainous terrains as a demonstration pilot. (iii) Support the Department of State Automobile Inspection under the Ministry of Interior, the lead agency for road safety, to develop a Road Safety Strategy and to establish a Road Safety Observatory.Component 3: Facilitate cross-border movement of goods (US$20 million equivalent). Two groups of activities will be financed under this component. (i) Upgrading of the Customs information and communication technology (ICT) platform (estimated at US$17.5 million), including equipment and facilities (computers, networking equipment, data center, end-use terminals), customs automation software, development and testing of the provided system, and implementation support up to 2025. (ii) Strengthening of institutional capacity and human resources in Customs Service (estimated at US$2.5 million), comprising integration of the newly upgraded Customs ICT platform with the National Single Window and other related systems, technical assistance on customs modernization, implementation of time release studies, assessment of implementation of measures under the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement, strengthening of the human resources unit within the Customs Service to ensure gender equality in employment and career promotion, and training of staff on code of ethics and gender-sensitivity to improve services to both female and male customers.Component 4: Support project implementation, coordination and management (US$2 million equivalent). This component will support project implementation, coordination and management including provision of goods, consultants services and training, operating costs and financial audit.Component 5: Contingent Emergency Response (US$0). This zero-dollar component is designed to provide swift response in the event of an eligible crisis or emergency, by enabling Tajikistan to request the World Bank to reallocate project funds to support emergency response, and reconstruction, where needed.

The Project development objectives of the Fourth Phase of the Central Asia Regional Links Program are to enhance the efficiency of cross-border trade for participants of the regional economy and to improve the resilience and safety of regional connectivity infrastructure in Sughd region and Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous region.The project contributes to the Central Asia Regional Links Programs higher-level development objectives of increasing cross-border connectivity and enhancing integrated regional development to revitalize historically active economic exchanges in Central Asia and beyond along the Silk Route.

title.narrative: Communities in target areas with effective citizen engagement channels

comment.narrative:
The indicator will measure the project & establishment of functioning channels for citizen engagement (that follow approved procedures) at the community (village or town) in the design/planning and monitoring of rehabilitation and construction of roads to ensure that local concerns and needs are addressed. Procedures will ensure, inclusion, and that the feedback loop is closed by MOT information and response. This indicator is being tied to the project GRM to ensure monitoring since the beginning of civil works contracts in Sughd and GBAO.
According to the data from the sociologist, there are 35 communities in Sughd and GBAO who benefit from the Project. Currently, the effective citizen engagement is established in all 35 communities in the construction works catchment area: 31 in Sughd and 4 in GBAO. That is 100% of total. The indicator has exceeded the target.

title.narrative: Market accessibility index of Sughd region

comment.narrative: This is an accessibility indicator for average access of the population to markets in Sughd region. From the beginning of the project, the formula from CARs-2 was used: H=?WJ/TIJ, where H is the accessibility indicator, W- is the size indicator at target j, such as total population in major cities (Khujand, Isfara, and Konibodom), and T is the travel time between the origin and target j, i.e in this case travel time to the market in Khujand from the nearby major cities. The baseline indicator at 20.99 was calculated with no end target for this indicator. There are three major cities in Sughd: Khujand, Isfara, and Konibodom. The baseline data for the first half of 2023 will be the following: Population of the major cities (thousand people): Khujand-198.7, Isfara-54.9, Konibodom-54.4 Total=308.0 (thousand persons) Travel time (in min): Khujand-10, Isfara-110, Konibodom-90 (min) Then, the baseline H would be 20.99, which should be updated in last ISR. The current value is 21.80.

title.narrative: Climate resilient structure constructed in project areas in GBAO

comment.narrative:
The total number of km of all bridges, tunnels and galleries constructed for climate resilience in GBAO under the project.
The road construction process is underway, As of November 30, 2024, the overall physical progress in GBAO is 58.1%. The works will be completed by spring 2026. Most likely the indicator will be achieved.

Targets shall be update upon completion of rehabilitation. Construction work is in progress on the road sections No 1, 2, 3, & 4, and the roads have been partially rehabilitated. The lower layer of asphalt pavement has been laid. At the same time, construction work is in progress to install curbstones, assemble precast reinforced concrete trays, install reinforced concrete pipes, construct embankments, excavate trenches, construct roadbeds, dismantle existing structures, relocate utility lines, construct the lower and upper layers of the foundation, and work is underway to install outdoor lighting supports. With 46.0% of works completed in Sughd, roads will be fully rehabilitated by spring 2026. Most likely the indicator will be achieved.

title.narrative: Size of road network with baseline geometry, location, condition, traffic volume, and natural hazard exposure data are collected

comment.narrative:
Ministry of Transport will collect baseline data of Tajikistan's road network, covering geometry, location, condition and traffic volume, to utilize them in the Road Asset Management System. It will collect data from all international roads by end of 2022, all national roads by end of 2024, and additional roads by end of 2026.
The Corporate Solutions Company in cooperation with the RAMS Department of the State Unitary Enterprise "Center for Digitalization of the Transport Sector" has started data collection. Currently, data was collected for 4,700 km (3,268 km of international and 1,432 km of national roads). Most likely the indicator will be achieved.

title.narrative: Road construction jobs created for the local community

comment.narrative:
Under civil works contracts, create opportunities for labor from local communities to be employed under the project.
During the reporting period, the total number of temporary jobs created for the local communities were 718, including 279 jobs in the construction of roads in GBAO and 469 jobs in the Sughd region. The indicator has exceeded the target.

title.narrative: Average daily traffic volume passing through Khorog Bridge

comment.narrative:
Traffic volume passing through Khorog Bridge, measuring the improvement of regional connectivity as well as increased trade and travel in GBAO, resulting from reduced transport and trip delays.
The bridge construction work is in progress. According to the data provided by the Department of Road Management of GBAO, the average daily traffic density on the section near the Khorog Bridge for the end of November 2024 is 1382.00 vehicles per day. Most likely the indicator will be achieved.

title.narrative: Road closures per year in Barsem caused by natural hazards

comment.narrative:
Annual number of hours of road closures in Barsem caused by natural hazards, measuring the resilience of transport and trade.
The baseline of this indicator was identified from the moment when this road was completely closed for a month due to the consequences of natural disasters that occurred. During the winter 2023-2024, based on the data provided by the State Road Maintenance Administration (GUSAD) of the Shugnan district, there were no roads closures in the village of Barsem due to natural and climatic conditions.

title.narrative: Adoption of a National Road Safety Strategy

comment.narrative: The contract for consultancy services for the development of the "National Road Safety Strategy for 2024-2034" between the Ministry of Transport and FRED Engineering S.r.I. was singed on July 31, 2024. The project started on August 9, 2024, and is expected to complete in 12 months. According to the initial report of FRED Engineering S.r.I., the project will be implemented in four stages to achieve the set goal. Currently, work is underway within the second stage, i.e. assessment of the current situation. It is planned to prepare a draft of the NRSS and AP 2024-2034 by August 2025. Adoption is planned for 2026. Most likely the indicator will be achieved

title.narrative: Preparation of five-year and annual road maintenance plan and budget

comment.narrative: Data for the preparation of the five-year and annual plan for road maintenance and budgeting will be analyzed in the HDM-4 software package. In September 2024, 5 licenses of HDM-4 software were purchased under the project. Currently, a survey of road user costs and a survey in road maintenance departments are being conducted, after which the HDM-4 software will be calibrated for Tajikistan in February 2025. Most likely the indicator will be achieved.
